name: OfficialUSA
tip: Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE to see its records for your name. If one is you, open it and copy its link. Then tap START OPT-OUT. Give your email, plus the link and your address if the form asks, then pick your record and tap Remove. It usually takes up to 48 hours. Its sister site Xlek needs its own opt-out. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Xlek (sister site of OfficialUSA)
tip: Search your first and last name on this page, tap the result that is you and choose opt-out. Each result needs its own request, and some take longer than others to verify. If the page shows a time-out error, their server is down, so try again later. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: SearchBug
tip: You do not need to find your record first. On this page tap Submit Opt-Out Request. In the form choose Opt-Out Request as the reason, type Do Not Sell as the subject and give your name, email and phone number. In the message box type your mailing address so they can find your record. Type the security code and tap Submit. An opt-out needs no ID, so skip any file upload.

name: Persopo (also People-search.org)
tip: Persopo takes removal requests by email and wants the listing's details, not a link. Search your name and state on the site. If a listing is you, tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST and add the age and relatives that listing shows, or paste its text. This also clears People-search.org, which Persopo owns. They say 10 to 20 business days. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: StateRecords.org
tip: Public records site from the company behind InfoTracer. It now takes removal requests by email. Tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST: the email gives your first and last name, city and state, which is what they ask for. Send it, then tap MARK AS SENT. If they have not confirmed after 15 days, tap EMAIL AGAIN.

name: CourtRecords.us (and its state sites)
tip: Court records site from the company behind InfoTracer, with state sites built from it. It now takes removal requests by email. Tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST: the email gives your first and last name, city and state, which is what they ask for, and asks them to clear their related sites too. Send it, then tap MARK AS SENT. If they have not confirmed after 15 days, tap EMAIL AGAIN.

name: BlockShopper (home sales)
tip: Publishes who bought and sold homes. If you have never bought or sold a home, tap NOT LISTED. Otherwise search your name on the site. If you are there, copy that page's link and tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST: the link goes in the email. BlockShopper says it only takes sale records down for officials, police and people with a protection order or a documented threat, so it may refuse.

name: Arity (Allstate driving data)
tip: Allstate's driving-data company. Texas sued it in 2025 for collecting drivers' data through phone apps without telling them. Fill in the form with your email and phone number, plus your phone's advertising ID if you still have one, then submit.

name: Unacast (location data, now with Gravy Analytics)
tip: Location data company that merged with Gravy Analytics. Fill in the opt-out and delete form, adding your phone's advertising ID if you still have one. If the form will not work, tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST instead.

name: Mobilewalla (location data)
tip: Location data company. Its form cannot work without your phone's advertising ID (in Settings, search for Ads). If you deleted that ID after the Kochava step, they have nothing to match, so tap NOT LISTED. Otherwise choose Deletion, enter your email and the ID, pick your country and state, tick that you are asking for yourself, solve the CAPTCHA and submit.

name: Dun & Bradstreet (business data)
tip: The oldest business-data company. It sells contact details for people tied to businesses. Ask to delete your data and to opt out of its sale, fill in your details and submit, then follow any email they send.

name: Verizon (if it is your carrier)
tip: Verizon uses your browsing and app data for ads under Custom Experience and Custom Experience Plus. Sign in and turn both off. In the My Verizon app it is under Me, Profile & Settings, My Profile. Or call 866-211-0874 and press 2. If Verizon is not your carrier, tap NOT LISTED.

name: AT&T and Cricket (if it is your carrier)
tip: No sign-in needed. Tick both boxes: opt out of sharing and selling, and opt out of the Personalized program. Fill in your name, email, phone and address and tap Submit. Or call 866-385-3193. If AT&T or Cricket is not your carrier, tap NOT LISTED.

name: T-Mobile and Metro (if it is your carrier)
tip: Sign in to the Privacy Dashboard, choose Manage Do Not Sell or Share and slide the toggles to OFF. Turn off any advertising sharing toggles you see there too. If T-Mobile or Metro is not your carrier, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Do Not Call Registry (sales calls)
tip: The government's free list that tells telemarketers to stop calling you. Register your cell number, then tap the link they email you to finish. It never expires. Sales calls should stop within 31 days. Scammers ignore it, but legal sellers must obey it.

name: Google: clear results for removed listings
tip: Use this after a site removes you but Google still shows the old result. Sign in, paste that result's link and tap Submit. If the page still exists, Google asks for a word or two that was in the old result and is gone now, such as your last name. Tap MARK AS DONE once you have sent every link you found.

name: Bing: clear results for removed listings
tip: The same clean-up for Bing. Sign in with a Microsoft account and paste the old result's link. Choose the page removal option if that link is now dead, or the outdated cache option if the page still opens without you, then type a word that used to be on it, such as your last name. Submit. Tap MARK AS DONE once you have sent every link you found.

name: Google: personalized ads off
tip: Stops Google using your activity to target ads on Google and on partner sites and apps. Sign in, set Personalized ads to Off and confirm. It applies to every device where you are signed in.
